text:
maria: quick q — trying to override a subchart map via --set-file but it isn't picked up in the rendered templates. Command I ran:

```
helm upgrade --install myapp ./charts/umbrella --set-file subA.config=./overrides.yaml
```

umbrella values.yaml has: `subA:` (map) and subchart template does: `{{- toYaml .Values.subA.config | nindent 8 }}`. After templating I still see the original default map, not the overrides.yaml contents. Is --set-file not supposed to replace maps?

aj: --set-file will set the value to the literal contents of the file (as a string). If the subchart expects a map, Helm won't parse that string into a map for you. So `toYaml` on a string won't behave like merging a YAML map. For structured overrides use a values file (or explicit --set key paths).

tim: also double-check whether the subchart uses a global/alias path. If the chart reads `{{ .Values.global.image.tag }}` or `{{ .Values.image.tag }}` instead of `{{ .Values.subA.image.tag }}`, then overriding `subA.config` won't affect it. Two common fixes: 1) put the map under the exact key the chart reads (e.g. global: { ... }) in a values file, or 2) change the subchart to use `{{ .Values.subA... }}` if you control it.

aj: quick examples:

- to supply a structured map: create overrides.yaml with `subA:` at top level, then `helm upgrade --install myapp ./charts/umbrella -f overrides.yaml`
- or override a single scalar: `--set subA.image.tag=canary`

maria: ah OK — I used --set-file because I thought it would merge YAML. I moved the YAML under top-level `subA:` and passed it with `-f overrides.yaml` and it works. Also found the subchart was reading `global` keys, so I had to set `global.image.tag` instead for one value.

helm-bot: FYI `helm template --debug` helped show the final .Values being rendered (useful for debugging overrides). :thumbsup:
